misconceptions.description: Assuming dry adhesion works without meaningful interface physics
misconceptions.trigger: learner treats dry adhesion as if it simply sticks by magic
misconceptions.feedback: Dry adhesion still depends on real contact mechanics, compliance, and intermolecular interactions. The absence of liquid glue does not mean the interface is simple.

misconceptions.description: Assuming smaller patterns automatically guarantee better adhesion
misconceptions.trigger: learner claims nanostructures always improve attachment regardless of context
misconceptions.feedback: Pattern scale must match the target surfaces, materials, loading direction, and durability requirements. Smaller is not automatically better.

misconceptions.description: Thinking reversible attachment cannot also be strong
misconceptions.trigger: learner assumes a reusable adhesive must have poor load capacity
misconceptions.feedback: A well-designed dry adhesive can be strong in one loading mode and still release cleanly in another. Directionality and contact design are critical.
